6395.summary: Internal SSA Risk Assessment Form dated June 16 2025 found 35-65% probability of data breach with catastrophic adverse effect after DOGE uploaded NUMIDENT to unsecured AWS cloud
6395.detail: Lead #18292. Source: Peters HSGAC Minority Staff Report DOGE_REPORT_FINAL_7.pdf released 2025-09-26. Also: Chuck Borges whistleblower disclosure 2025-08-26.

6413.summary: Peters report warned worst-case NUMIDENT breach could require re-issuing Social Security numbers for all 548M+ Americans, triggering mass identity theft and disrupting banking, employment, healthcare, and housing
6413.detail: Lead #18292. NUMIDENT contains all data submitted in SSN applications for 300M+ living Americans and additional deceased persons. Total SSNs issued: 548.3M+ as of early August 2025. Breach would expose data to foreign adversaries Russia, China, and Iran which regularly probe US networks.

6476.summary: On April 8, 2025, SSA added 6,300+ living immigrants to the Death Master File (also renamed 'Ineligible Master File'). The list came from DHS — immigrants whose temporary legal status had just been revoked, reportedly including individuals flagged as terrorist watchlist or FBI criminal records. Aram Moghaddassi described the list as immigrants 'homeland security officials had identified as having temporary legal status but who were now either on the terrorist watch list or had FBI criminal records.' The 6,300 additions used synthetic/fabricated death dates. The list included minors, including a child as young as 13. Career IT chief Greg Pearre was physically removed from his office for opposing the plan as illegal. Acting Commissioner Leland Dudek signed two memoranda with DHS Secretary Kristi Noem authorizing the action despite initially believing it was illegal.
